activity.text: For most of my 30+ years in international pharma, "going global" very often meant one company trying to be excellent everywhere at once. It rarely worked evenly. What's shifting is the assumption underneath it: that a company has to own a market to serve it well. Take an emerging biopharma - a biotech or small pharma with a strong product and no footprint in Europe. Whether it's based in Boston, Hyderabad, Singapore or Dubai, the old choice was binary: build a local affiliate, or leave the market on the table for years. Partnership models make both unnecessary. A specialist already on the ground holds the authorisation and runs operations; the company keeps its product, its brand and its upside, and reaches patients in a fraction of the time. Switzerland is the clearest case I know. Standing up a Swiss affiliate for a handful of products rarely adds up, yet its value per patient is among the highest anywhere. A partner already holding the Marketing Authorisation closes that gap in months, not years. That's a big part of how Agnes Wasem and I think about building WALue Pharma. #MarketAccess #SwissPharma #PharmaStrategy #WALuePharma

Last weekend, between Art Basel openings, I sat in on an IMD session "Built Different: Art, Entrepreneurship and the New Logic of Value." One idea stayed with me long after. In art, value rarely comes from the cost of the materials. It is created through scarcity, provenance, meaning, trust, and relevance. Increasingly, the same is true in business. Many of today's most valuable assets are intangible: expertise, trust, networks, reputation, the ability to execute. I have spent over 30 years in international pharma, much of it with in-market and mature brands, and nowhere is this clearer. A medicine is too often judged only by its growth rate and patent status. Yet some products remain critical to patient care after launch, their value held not in revenue alone, but in the trust they have earned among physicians, pharmacists, patients and health systems. The harder discipline for an entrepreneur is not identifying value. It is recognising it where others have stopped looking, whether in a mature brand, a stalled launch, or a market everyone overlooks. A timely reminder that value creation is as much about perspective as performance. It is a big part of why Agnes Wasem and I built WALue Pharma. #ArtBasel #IMD #Entrepreneurship #Healthcare #ValueCreation #Leadership #WALuePharma

Switzerland is often treated as a small European market. While representing only a fraction of Europe's population, Switzerland consistently ranks among the most attractive pharmaceutical markets in the world. Yet many companies underestimate its complexity. Success here requires mastering a combination of factors rarely found elsewhere: • A distinct regulatory framework through Swissmedic • Premium pricing dynamics and reference pricing implications • Rapid access decisions compared with many European markets • High scientific influence among healthcare professionals • Stringent quality and pharmacovigilance requirements The challenge is that these elements cannot be managed in isolation. Regulatory approval without market access is insufficient. Market access without local operational infrastructure creates risk. Commercial ambition without compliance is simply unsustainable. After spending decades in Pharma, I have learned that success comes from connecting regulatory, quality, market access and commercial execution into one coherent operating model. That is precisely why Switzerland rewards preparation and execution more than almost any other market. www.walue-pharma.com #WALuePharma #SwissPharma #Swissmedic #MarketAccess #CommercialStrategy

Today is a significant day for me. After 30 years in global pharma, from research scientist to commercial strategist, from Novartis to PE-backed platform builds, one thing has become clear: The best pharmaceutical businesses are never built alone. They are built by great teams, trusted partners, and an unwavering focus on execution. That belief is at the heart of WALue Pharma. Switzerland is not a compliance problem. It is one of Europe's most attractive pharmaceutical markets, with a distinct regulatory framework, premium pricing environment, strong HCP influence. Building a platform that truly performs here: commercially, operationally, and compliantly - requires a different level of expertise. Agnes Wasem and I founded WALue Pharma after decades of building, operating and optimizing pharmaceutical businesses. We know what success looks like because we have delivered it ourselves. WALue Pharma is not another service provider. We offer a fully integrated Swiss platform covering Market Authorisation Holder responsibilities, regulatory affairs, pharmacovigilance, quality, market access, and commercial operations - backed by experienced scientific and commercial professionals with deep Swiss market expertise. Today, we go live. If Switzerland is on your agenda, I would welcome a conversation. #WALuePharma #SwissPharma #MarketEntry #CommercialExcellence #Swissmedic #PharmaSwitzerland

Thirty years in the pharmaceutical industry gives perspective. I have worked across large organizations and more entrepreneurial environments, and one thing has remained constant: the quality of the people around the table makes all the difference. Over the years I have had the privilege to work with many exceptional women: colleagues, leaders, mentors who bring rigor, perspective and resilience to the organizations they help shape. I now see the same strength and ambition in the next generation, including my daughter Maxine Akyel--Albientz an ESSEC student, which makes me incredibly proud. One key observation: diversity around the table matters. It brings structure to complex conversations, helps create balance and ultimately leads to better decisions. Progress on gender equality in the workplace is real, but we are not there yet. Continuing to build environments where talent can develop and lead remains an important responsibility for all of us. On International Women’s Day, I simply want to recognize the many women who contribute every day to moving things forward. #InternationalWomensDay

Thank you NEXT Pharma for the invitation. In today’s environment, value in pharma is no longer created by scale alone. It is earned through disciplined capital allocation, lifecycle optimization, and operating precision across the full value chain. Specialty platforms demand clarity of strategy, governance alignment, and execution rigor. Sustainable performance comes from making the right choices under constraints. I look forward to discussing how we can build resilient organizations that create durable value for patients and stakeholders alike. See you in Dubrovnik!

Back from Davos after a series of focused discussions on governance, decision-making and much more. Across the IMD board breakfast, the World Woman Foundation and the Female Quotient, the message was consistent: in the boardroom, influence is built less on airtime and more on judgment, clarity, and the ability to navigate complex trade-offs. Value is created through disciplined challenge, trust, and long-term stewardship. A brief pause from execution to exchange perspectives with peers.

This year has reinforced a simple truth: when things get difficult, discipline matters more than narrative. I spend part of the year in situations where speed was expected, opinions were loud, and certainty was in short supply. In those moments, the most useful skill turned out to be knowing when not to react. Not every issue requires momentum. Not every discussion needs alignment. Not every tension demands resolution. Choosing where to slow down, where to listen longer, and where to let outcomes play out was the real lever. Carrying that discipline into what comes next.

New frontier for Gubra! We have initiated the first-in-human Phase 1/2a clinical trial of GUB-UCN2 (a long-acting urocortin-2 analog), one of our proprietary development products in obesity, with the first participant having completed the first study visit. GUB-UCN2 is part of a promising new therapeutic class with Gubra at the forefront of advancing this emerging field. For us, this is much more than the start of another clinical study. It represents the beginning of clinical development for what we believe could become an entirely new frontier of obesity treatment with the potential to improve body composition by selectively reducing fat mass while preserving and building muscle. At Gubra, our ambition is to build a compelling pipeline of highly differentiated, high-value clinical assets with the potential to transform patient care. GUB-UCN2 is an important step in delivering on that strategy, and we believe its potential extends well beyond obesity alone. The ambitious Phase 1/2a study is designed to generate a rich, multidimensional clinical dataset by evaluating GUB-UCN2 both as a standalone therapy and in combination with incretin-based treatments, while also providing early insights into muscle volume and muscle function. This approach lays the foundation for exploring multiple patient populations and future indications. GUB-UCN2 has already demonstrated compelling preclinical data, including: • Selective substantial reduction of fat mass with increases in muscle mass • Prevention and even reversal of lean mass loss associated with GLP-1-based therapies • Improvements in cardiac and renal function in preclinical models These findings give us confidence that GUB-UCN2 has the potential to become a highly differentiated therapeutic candidate. The future of obesity treatment is not simply about losing weight, it is about building healthier body composition by losing the right weight and weight maintenance. I am proud of our outstanding teams at Gubra whose scientific excellence, commitment, and passion have made this milestone possible. Thank you to everyone making this journey possible. The journey has just begun, and we look forward to sharing the first clinical data in 2027. Read more: https://lnkd.in/d-qa6K-C #Gubra #Biotech #ClinicalTrials #Phase1 #Obesity #MuscleHealth #BodyComposition #PeptideTherapeutics #DrugDiscovery #Innovation #LifeSciences #MetabolicDisease #CRHR2 #UCN2 #HealthyWeightLoss Note: GUB-UCB2 is in development and has not received a marketing authorisation in any jurisdiction.

activity.text: 🚨 NEWS ALERT: German healthcare group Fresenius Group has created a corporate venture capital unit that plans to invest more than €200 million in healthcare startups over the next five years. 🤔 Why it matters: The fund adds more than €200 million of potential strategic capital to a difficult European healthcare financing market. It also signals that Fresenius wants to engage with emerging technologies earlier, potentially creating a new route to partnerships, licensing deals and acquisitions for young biotechs. 🔧 How it works: The fund will invest from early financing rounds through the growth stage, targeting areas adjacent to Fresenius’ three strategic platforms: biopharma, medtech and care provision. 🔎 Zoom in: Fresenius has appointed Thomas Michael Thestrup to lead the new unit. Thestrup joins from Angelini Ventures , the corporate venture arm of Italy’s Angelini Industries. His previous positions include business development and strategy roles at Lundbeck and UCB , as well as life sciences investing at Danish venture firm Sunstone Life Science Ventures . ✅ Don’t miss the next biotech story from European Biotechnology Magazine Subscribe here: https://lnkd.in/e5KjDRmt
